versions.name: RXV2-0.9.748-page-load-order
versions.notes: Seven tuning pages have been dead since 0.9.742 this morning - PIDs, PID +, Rates, Governor (profile), Rescue, Easy tuning and Copy a bank: no bank buttons, no Save, nothing (Malcolm 2026-09-17: 'the copy from and the copy to boxes are both empty!', on Android and iPhone alike). One mistake, made seven times: app.js is loaded 'deferred', which means it runs AFTER a page's own script, and the six-bank change put a call into app.js at the very top of each page's script - so the page's whole script died before it defined anything. Every one is fixed by doing that work when the page has finished loading instead. The same fault was found lying in wait on the Fly page, where the status card had sat at '...' for ever, so that is fixed too. And a new gate now runs each page's script exactly as the browser does, before app.js exists, and refuses to publish anything that breaks - it caught all eight. Pages only; nothing changes in the air.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.747-ride-out-drops
versions.notes: Malcolm's 'crash' was not a crash (2026-09-17): 'the app returned to the opening screen, but the model wasn't selectable'. The Bluetooth link had dropped mid-session, and both apps treated any drop outside a reboot they had asked for as 'the model was switched off' and went straight to the scanner - with auto-connect disarmed, while the receiver was still tearing the old link down, so a tap on the model went nowhere. Now any unexpected drop from a live link is ridden out: 30 seconds of quiet reconnecting (90 for a reboot the app asked for), and if that window closes the scanner opens with auto-connect ARMED, so the receiver connects by itself the moment it is seen again. A model that really was switched off still lands on the scanner promptly. The receiver now logs WHY a link dropped (the radio's own reason code: lost each other, the phone ended it, we ended it), so the next one is diagnosable from the log alone. Firmware change is that one log line; nothing changes in the air.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.746-ble-request-ids
versions.notes: Three faults from one Bluetooth session on RAW420AJB (Malcolm 2026-09-17: the app crashed on the update screen, it said there was no WiFi beside the router at -33 dBm, and no update was offered although 0.9.745 was out). The receiver's own log settled the WiFi one at once: its WiFi never dropped. The real fault was in the Bluetooth bridge, which had NO way of tying a reply to a request. When the app gave up on a slow request (4 s) and sent the next, the receiver silently threw the new one away - it was still inside the old handler - and then delivered the OLD reply, which the app took as the answer to the NEW request; every reply after that was one behind. The update page received some other endpoint's reply in place of state.json, found no WiFi field in it, and said 'no WiFi here'. That wrong answer was then remembered as the pilot's own choice of lane and forced the install down Bluetooth. Fixed properly: every request now carries a number, the receiver echoes it in the reply, and a reply for a request the app has given up on is swallowed and dropped, never handed to the wrong one. The receiver also refuses to send a reply nobody is waiting for. Old apps and old receivers keep working unchanged. The update offer: the front page's check asked only the receiver, whose WiFi cannot reach the internet while Bluetooth holds the radio, and took 'both sources failed' as a final answer - it now asks the phone's own internet first, as the update page always did. The crash: nothing readable was left behind, so the Android app now writes every crash to a file and shows it on the next launch with a Copy button; and two things that could have been it are fixed regardless - a dead web view was destroyed from inside its own callback (an Android-documented crash), and an out-of-memory during a Bluetooth install had no handler at all. Also: the armed-banner poll shares the page's own state read over Bluetooth instead of doubling it. Nothing changes in the air - Bluetooth is off when armed.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.745-park-a-bank
versions.notes: Copy a bank now shows EVERY bank the flight controller has, even the ones you have hidden with How many banks (Malcolm 2026-09-17: "our copy bank function should allow all banks even if we don't use them all. That will allow a bank to be parked so it can be restored after an unsuccessful experiment"). Copy the tune you are happy with into a bank you never fly before you start changing things; if the experiment goes badly, copy it back and you are exactly where you were - quicker than a full restore, and it survives the flying session. Parking would be useless if the parking space were hidden, so this one page deliberately ignores the cap, and says so on the page when you have banks hidden, because otherwise the extra buttons look like a fault. The tuning pages are unchanged: they still show only what you said you use. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.744-banks-profiles
versions.notes: Malcolm's final wording: "How many banks (Profiles) do you use (1-6)?" - Rotorflight's own word for a bank is a profile, and the house rule is plain English first with the firmware's jargon in brackets, so anyone who has read Rotorflight's documentation knows at once which thing is meant. The range shown is the range that flight controller really offers. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.743-banks-wording
versions.notes: Malcolm's wording for the new setting: "How many banks do you use (1-6)?" rather than the bare label "How many banks" - it is a question put to the pilot, so it should read like one. The range in it is the range that flight controller really offers, so a smaller board asks (1-3). Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.742-six-banks
versions.notes: Rotorflight has SIX banks, not four (Malcolm 2026-09-17: "we ought to enable 6. Maybe we should add an option 'How many banks' which allows up to six"). Every tuning page offered four, so banks 5 and 6 were out of reach - and worse, the phone's Back up never saved them and never restored them, silently, with the progress bar reading 100 %. Both are fixed, and nothing assumes a number any more: the flight controller is asked how many it has (MSP 101), because Rotorflight builds the count from flash size and the two counts can differ - a full-size board has 6 PID and 6 rate banks, a smaller one 3 PID but still 6 rate. A new setting on the Rotorflight page, How many banks, caps what the pages show for a pilot who only uses a few; it is kept on the receiver, so it follows the model from phone to phone. One rule it can never break: it may hide a bank you do not use, but never the bank the flight controller is actually ON - if your switch selects bank 5 while you have asked for three, the page shows bank 5 anyway, because editing a bank you cannot see is how a tune gets lost. A remembered bank is clamped too, so a stale bank 5 cannot leave a three-bank flight controller lighting nothing. Also fixed: the adjustments page could not express 'in bank 5' at all; Copy a bank said 'copying from bank 4' when the flight controller was on 5 or 6. All seven bank rows are now drawn by one piece of code, so there is one place to get this right. New check in the publish gate: 14 cases covering caps, small boards, stale banks and the never-hide rule - publishing refuses if any fails. Apps 5.81 (iOS) / 5.73 (Android) carry the six-bank backup. Nothing changes in the air: all of this is disarmed, on the ground.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.741-help-audit
versions.notes: Every help screen re-read for things that are no longer true (Malcolm 2026-09-17: 'please re read all help text and look for out of date bits we ought to fix'). Four independent readers went through all 50 pages against the code that actually runs, and about 40 corrections came out of it. The ones that mattered most: Back up said a tune from a friend's helicopter brings his stick setup, channel map and bank switches with it - it does NOT any more (that is his radio, not his tune), and it only saves banks 1-4; the black box help mixed up the receiver's own flight record with the flight controller's black box - two different things; the swash trims were called tenths of a degree everywhere when Rotorflight means percent of servo throw; the update page told Android users to use 'the iPhone app'. Travel extents said everything twice - its help had been appended rather than merged - and Control sense and Collective up/down balance had no help at all; the dongle and Receiver settings help panels opened halfway down themselves. Three stale comments in the phone apps' own source were fixed too, including two that named the wrong selector slots. Pages and comments only - nothing changes in the air.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.740-one-app
versions.notes: Every page's help now says it plainly (Malcolm 2026-09-17): this is ONE app and ONE firmware for both boards. At every power-up the board looks for its transceivers - found, it is a receiver and flies the model; none, it is a dongle and only sets up the flight controller. That is why the pages look almost the same either way, and why a dongle simply hides the few that need a radio. Someone handed a dongle has no reason to guess any of that. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.739-help-words
versions.notes: Fixes a fault in this morning's own change (Malcolm asked whether the help screens needed checking too - they did). The help panels ARE corrected on a dongle, which is right, but a sentence that already mentioned both boards had the word swapped in it as well: 'USB-C cable, receiver or dongle to the flight controller' came out as 'dongle or dongle'. Now any sentence that already names a dongle is left completely alone - it was written knowing about both - which fixes that and also makes it safe to phrase a sentence for both boards wherever one is genuinely about both. Everywhere else each reader still sees their own word: a receiver says receiver, a dongle says dongle. 39 test cases. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.738-says-dongle
versions.notes: On a dongle the pages now say dongle wherever they mean the dongle (Malcolm 2026-09-17: 'it often says receiver when a dongle should say dongle'). There were about 190 mentions, so instead of a list of phrases to change - which could never stay complete - the word is simply swapped, except in a sentence where receiver means something else: Rotorflight's own 'serial receiver' port function, the configurator's Receiver tab, the Ports page's receiver choices, and above all 'the receiver that flies the model', which is a different thing entirely and must never be renamed. A sentence like that is left completely alone, so the worst this can do is leave the old wording. It also watches the page, so the words written after it loads - progress lines, refusals, banners - are corrected too. 35 test cases: 17 swapped, 18 protected. Pages only.

versions.name: RXV2-0.9.737-one-installer
versions.notes: Only one piece of code installs an update now (Malcolm 2026-09-17: 'we seem to have multiple places that install updates. One gives byte count, one does not. I suggest only one bit of code should update so we only ever need to update that bit'). The front page carried its own copy, which had drifted: no byte count, no choice of WiFi or Bluetooth, no three-minute grace before calling an install failed, and a different failure message. Its 'Update now?' offer now opens the update page and installs from there - 117 lines of duplicate gone, and the one remaining installer is the better one. Pages only.

rotorflight.line: Rotorflight 2.3 — the release these pages are written and tested against.
